works.citation: Martin Pâquet, Tracer les marges de la Cité: étranger, immigrant et État au Québec, 1627-1981 (Montréal: Boréal, 2005).

verification.checked_against: Review headings: Bruno Ramirez, Recherches sociographiques 47:2 (2006), doi:10.7202/014231ar ('Montréal, Les Éditions du Boréal, 2005, 317 p.'); Chedly Belkhodja, Politique et Sociétés 25:1 (2006), doi:10.7202/013523ar ('Boréal, 2005, 328 p.'); Hélène Pellerin, Études internationales 38:1 (2007), doi:10.7202/015724ar; Open Library OL11444104W; publisher-supplied description on Perlego (2010 ebook).
verification.note: Description read: Pâquet studies the categories of 'Étranger' and 'Immigrant' from 1627 to 1981; three types of categories succeed one another, ending in a contractual representation of the political community. A search summary also gave the endpoints (Compagnie des Cent-Associés 1627; Quebec ministry of cultural communities and immigration 1981) and the three category types (allegiance, origin/ethnicity, economic actor); these details were not read on a primary page. Book unread.

context.francophone_universe: 179 of 1303 in-analysis PhDs (2009-2026) are at montreal (91), uqam (65), sherbrooke (14), laval (9). Laval is badly undercounted (download still open), which matters because Pâquet teaches there.
context.francophone_immigration_phds: Few francophone PhDs in the corpus are about immigration or ethnicity in Quebec: e.g. UQAM 2016 Roy (Japanese community of Quebec, 1942-1988); Montréal 2021 Vigliano (recent Italian women immigrants in Montreal); Montréal 2022 Belony (memory of Duvalierism in Montreal's Haitian diaspora); UQAM 2019 Balloud (French clergy in migration to Canada). These few theses drive most francophone counts above.
context.what_francophone_theses_cite: Roy 2016 and Vigliano 2021 cite the English-Canadian canon (Knowles, Backhouse, Kelley and Trebilcock, Avery, Roy, Iacovetta) alongside Pâquet 2005, Ramirez 1984/1991, Helly 1987, Anctil 1988, Taschereau 1987/1988 and Linteau 2000. The francophone literature is used, but by a handful of theses.

recommendation.strand_suggestion: A short 'Immigration to Quebec' strand: Ramirez (1984, 1991) and Helly (1987) on Italian and Chinese Montrealers, Anctil (1988) on Jewish Montreal and French-Canadian responses, Taschereau's 1988 RHAF call to move immigration history beyond community 'ghettos', and Pâquet on how the Quebec state defined the immigrant (1997; 2005).
recommendation.wording_caution: Do not say these works were widely taken up: in the 2009-2026 PhD corpus each is cited by 2-8 dissertations. Pâquet 2005 is the only one with a majority of francophone citing theses.

qids.qid_note: Anctil and Linteau found by MCP vector search; Pâquet, Ramirez, Helly and Taschereau not returned by vector search, found by exact-label SPARQL through the MCP and checked with get_statements (Pâquet: historian, Laval, b. 1963; Ramirez: historian, Université de Montréal, b. 1942; Helly: b. 1943, INRS Centre Urbanisation Culture Société; Taschereau: historian, UQTR, educated UQAM; her authorship of the 1987/1988 works is inferred, not stated in Wikidata).
